Natisha Hiedeman’s leadership and offense shine in Seattle
summary_text: SEATTLE — Storm guard Natisha Hiedeman is well known by most WNBA fans for her off-court activities, as one half of the beloved Studbudz. She and Courtney Williams recently pulled off another 72-hour livestream over WNBA All-Star weekend as part of their joint venture. But how she has elevated her game on the court for Seattle this season warrants more recognition. Shortly after another successful stream, on Tuesday, Hiedeman was back on the court in Seattle. Hair still strikingly blue, matching Williams for All-Star, Hiedeman scored a career-high 33 points on 55% shooting, and added six rebounds and four assists, in a loss to the Indiana Fever, taking more shots to make up for the absence of injured All-Star Dominique Malonga . The performance showed off every part of her game, not just top-tier passing and 3-point shooting, but also impressive midrange, downhill driving, nice shooting touch and elite handles.

title: Napheesa Collier plays on her home court for first time in 2026
summary_text: MINNEAPOLIS — In arguably the most popular song ever written about the concept of waiting — ‘The Waiting’ by Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers — every day, seeing just one more card is one of several elements that makes waiting the hardest part. For Minnesota Lynx fans, that translates to more than 300 cards to demonstrate how long they’ve waited to watch Napheesa Collier play on the Target Center floor again. Fans across the state of Minnesota had memories and faith to help them while they waited to hear Collier’s name again. It was last announced in the Lynx’s starting lineup in front of the home crowd in Game 2 of the 2025 WNBA Playoff Semifinals, 308 days ago.

summary_text: Jessica Shepard and Arike Ogunbowale scored 15 points each and the Dallas Wings used a big run in the third quarter to cruise to an 83-63 win over the Connecticut Sun on Sunday night. After a slow start to the third quarter, when the Wings had more misses and turnovers than points, they followed a timeout with a 20-2 run to close the quarter and turn a nine-point lead into a 72-45 lead. The Sun went 3 of 15 from the field and scored just eight points.

title: Demonstrations and conversations from Sunday’s Fever at Lynx game in Minneapolis
summary_text: MINNEAPOLIS — Sunday’s matinee between the Minnesota Lynx and Indiana Fever at Target Center marked the first meeting of the season between the WNBA’s two highest-scoring teams. Indiana entered the day as winners of their last five games while eclipsing 100 points in all five, and boasting a league-best average of 96.4 points per game. Minnesota, winners of nine straight entering Sunday, held the second best scoring average of the league at 92.2, and eclipsed the century mark in five of the previous nine wins. Both offenses delivered with scorching hot performances on national television, with the Lynx outlasting the Fever 108-100. The 69 points between the teams in the first 10 minutes alone marked the highest-scoring first quarter in WNBA history . Olivia Miles and Kelsey Mitchell exchanged offensive firework displays throughout the afternoon. Mitchell’s 37 points fell just one shy of matching a career high. Miles set a franchise record for eclipsing 20 points and 5 assists for the 10th time in a single season, surpassing Lynx legend Maya Moore , who held that record with nine such games in 2015.

title: How the Phoenix Mercury’s 1997 reunion was a reflection for how much the team, league have grown
summary_text: PHOENIX — On June 22, 1997, Bridget Pettis scored the first points in Phoenix Mercury franchise history. No one knew what would become of the WNBA or the Mercury organization. Gas in the United States was roughly $1.20 per gallon; nobody had iPhones or social media. Nearly 30 years later, Pettis stood at center court before a sold-out arena, no longer introducing the franchise to the world but being celebrated as one of the women who made it possible.

She hugged her teammates and even threw in a few dance moves as Mystics fans stood and screamed and Wings fans raced for the exits. Then, as she waited for teammate Michaela Onyenwere to finish a television interview and for her own to start, McMahon made more “W” signs in the direction of a camera. It was like she couldn’t help it, with all her energy and pride in the Mystics’ performance suddenly having nowhere to go but into celebrating.

summary_text: UNCASVILLE, Conn. — Rayah Marshall was sitting in a movie theater watching the newly released “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” when she got the call to come back to the Connecticut Sun. She called the moment “perfect timing.” On Aug. 1, the Sun signed Marshall to a seven-day contract, but she didn’t know how chaotic her next 24 hours were going to be.

title: ‘It’s about pride’: How the Phoenix Mercury are coping with their playoff odds dwindling
summary_text: PHOENIX — When the Phoenix Mercury acquired Kelsey Plum on Aug. 1, it was seen as a move intended to spark life into a final playoff push just as much as it was a gamble on reshaping the team’s future . But in just five games since the trade, the Mercury have plummeted out of postseason contention. After going 2-3 during that stretch, including three losses in a row to the Atlanta Dream, Connecticut Sun and Washington Mystics, the Mercury find themselves seven games back of a playoff spot with only nine games to play.

title: ‘Erase your potential’: Inside the Washington Mystics’ player development process
summary_text: WASHINGTON — As one of the youngest teams in WNBA history , the Washington Mystics are considered a team with plenty of potential. But to player development lead Clinton Crouch, that’s almost a dirty word. “If someone’s talking about your potential, that means you’re not good yet; you just look like you might be good one day,” he told The IX Sports in May.

title: Minnesota is viewing its longest road trip of the season as a battle test and a sprint
summary_text: PORTLAND, Ore. — The Minnesota Lynx are treating the rest of their regular season schedule like it’s a sprint. A sprint split into two legs, bookending a multi-week WNBA break for the FIBA Women’s World Cup, but a sprint with an intermission still qualifies as a sprint. It’s the kind of sense of urgency head coach and president of basketball operations Cheryl Reeve says is imperative in order for the Lynx to enter the 2026 playoffs the right way. An aspect that may have been missing from last year’s championship pursuit.

title: Ta’Niya Latson is finding her confidence with the Las Vegas Aces
summary_text: To close out a five-game road trip, the Las Vegas Aces took on the New York Liberty on Sunday. After playing the Minnesota Lynx less than 24 hours beforehand, head coach Becky Hammon decided to bench three of her starters to let them rest for their homestand. That meant the rest of the team had to step up to the plate. With 5:47 left in the fourth quarter, Mai Yamamoto had the ball in the offensive zone. She found rookie development player, Ta’Niya Latson , and passed the ball her way. Standing behind the arc, she shot the ball before Liberty guard Marine Fauthoux could shoot the ball. The ball went over Fauthoux and straight into the basket.

title: Bridget Carleton, ‘an automatic No. 1’ for Portland, is just getting better
summary_text: PORTLAND, Ore. — The Portland Fire knew they wanted Bridget Carleton from the start. The Fire’s front office “zoomed in” on the former Minnesota Lynx rotation player early in the process, general manager Vanja Černivec told reporters following their expansion draft this April. “What we wanted was, from the roster, as I mentioned, our strategy was … to identify the one unrestricted free agent that we really want to get our hands on,” Černivec said. But there was a little more to it than that — the Fire also had to predict and navigate the picks of the second 2026 expansion team, the Toronto Tempo.

title: Back from injury, masked Ezi Magbegor brings defense and leadership to Seattle Storm
summary_text: SEATTLE — Ezi Magbegor signed the Storm’s largest contract in the offseason, worth $3,750,000 total over three years, to keep the only remaining member of the 2020 WNBA Championship-winning team in Seattle. That was her rookie season, and she was just 20 years old. Now 27 and in her seventh season with the Storm, the franchise hopes she can be the key younger-yet-veteran core of a rebuilding team. But for most of the season, her contributions have been contained to the sidelines as she dealt with injuries. Before the season started, Magbegor suffered a foot injury while playing for Australia in the 2026 FIBA Basketball World Cup Qualifiers in March. After 20 missed games, the center returned to the floor on July 2 at Phoenix. She played three games off the bench on a minutes restriction; then, in her fourth game back, she took a hit to the face in Atlanta and broke her nose. The facial injury and some related concussion symptoms meant she then missed another six games and the All-Star break, returning a second time on July 31 in the same city where she suffered the injury, now with a mask she will wear the rest of the season.

title: The IX Sports Podcast Basketball Edition: Stephanie White’s message and the WNBA’s fight for dignity
summary_text: This week on The IX Sports Podcast Basketball Edition, hosts Jackie Powell and Howard Megdal break down the WNBA’s fight for dignity, starting with Indiana Fever Head Coach Stephanie White’s Tuesday night statement . The pair played the statement in full on the episode, and it is also included below. White’s statement “This isn’t necessarily for those people that are in this room. This is more for an online community that’s trying to create narratives that simply don’t exist, trying to create a fabrication or distortion of who I am, of what I’m about. Our players’ success, our players’ health and wellness, our players’ safety is always a top priority for me. One of the things I pride myself on is my relationships with players,” White said before referencing reaction to a recent hard foul committed by Chicago Sky guard DiJonai Carrington against Sophie Cunningham on Saturday.

title: Tiffany Hayes is thriving in a veteran role with the Valkyries
summary_text: Tiffany Hayes’ most impactful season yet has also been one in which she has spent less time on the court than ever before. That’s okay with Hayes. When she returned to the Valkyries for a second season, she and the team understood what she needed to do to stay healthy and available. The result has been one of the most joyful seasons of her career.
